title: A picture of a walk shows the properties panel, not a white gap
goal: The scripted walks take two kinds of picture, and the one that always works shows the canvas but draws the whole right hand properties panel as blank white. Anyone reading a walk report on a machine that cannot record the screen sees a picture with the panel missing, so nothing about the panel can be checked from it.
notes: Measured on 2026-09-07 during the-mixed-one-look-walk task. Scripts/playtest.sh Scripts/playtest/mixed-one-look-walk.json writes 1-mixed-dock.png and 2-mixed-dock-lower.png with identical md5s while the -sc.png pair differ. The offscreen path is PlaytestHarness.snapshot(_:name:) around line 2885: bitmapImageRepForCachingDisplay + cacheDisplay on the window contentView. The dock is NOT a child window (only HintTooltip.swift adds one), so this is cacheDisplay failing to reproduce the dock hosting view, most likely a layer-backed / material subtree it cannot draw. Likely fix: render through the layer (CALayer.render(in:)) or an ImageRenderer of the dock hosting view, composited into the same bitmap. Docs already updated with the limitation in docs/design/playtest-harness.md.
acceptance: A walk snapshot taken with two layers picked shows the properties panel with its real controls, not a white column
Two snapshots taken either side of a panel scroll differ from each other
Existing walks that photograph the canvas look the same as before
